name: Toyota GR Supra
reliability: 8/10 — B58 is among BMW's toughest modern engines; some early oil consumption, but Toyota-like in practice
cost_to_own: Insurance: High (380hp sports coupe) · Maintenance ~$900/yr (BMW mechanicals, Toyota service network)
popular_mods: ECU tune (JB4 piggyback or MHD/bootmod3 flash) — 450-500+ whp potential
Downpipe, intake, charge pipe, upgraded intercooler
E85 for big power on the stock turbo (500+ whp)
Coilovers, sway bars, big brake kit
oil_interval: Every 5,000-7,500 miles (BMW's 10k+ interval is too long)

generations.A40/A60 (1978–1986): Celica Supra — the inline-six GT origins of the nameplate.
generations.A80 (1993–2002): Legendary 2JZ-GTE twin-turbo — 320hp stock, 1,000hp+ capable. The car that built the Supra legend.
generations.A90/A91 (2020–present): Revived after 17 years. BMW-derived B58 3.0 inline-six (335→382hp) and B48 2.0. Co-developed with BMW (Z4 sibling), built by Magna Steyr. Manual added 2023; Final Edition up to 429hp.

common_issues: Early-year oil consumption (piston rings) with occasional limp mode
Wind buffeting with windows down (cheap deflector fix)
It's BMW underneath — electronics, interior, and engine are BMW-sourced
maintenance_tips: Shorten oil intervals below BMW's 10k recommendation
Use BMW LL-spec oil — the B58 is particular
Balance and align wheels to cure highway steering shudder
Huge tuning headroom, but upgrade fueling before chasing big power

engine.detail: BMW's B58 3.0L single-turbo inline-six, 382 hp / 368 lb-ft - one of the toughest modern BMW engines and a huge tuning platform.
engine.watch: Early 2020-21 cars can drink oil and their plastic-ring oil pump can crack (metal from 2022+); shorten intervals well below BMW's 10k.

drivetrain.detail: RWD via a ZF 8-speed automatic (6-speed manual added 2023) with an active electronic limited-slip diff.
drivetrain.watch: The ZF auto is essentially bulletproof and shrugs off big power - nothing chronic to flag here.

suspension.detail: Adaptive dampers with struts up front and a multilink rear - sharp and composed for a GT.
suspension.watch: Some cars develop a highway-speed steering shudder, almost always cured by a proper wheel balance and alignment.

brakes.detail: Four-piston fixed front calipers on 348mm discs - strong, confident street stoppers.
brakes.watch: More than enough for the road; add track fluid and pads for repeated hard laps, but there's no inherent weakness.

fuel.detail: Single high-pressure direct-injection system feeding the B58.
fuel.watch: Stock fueling is the ceiling for big builds - add E85 or upgraded fueling before chasing 500+ whp.

body.detail: A Z4 sibling built by Magna Steyr in Austria - genuine BMW hardware under Toyota styling.
body.watch: Noticeable wind buffeting with the windows down; a cheap aftermarket deflector sorts it.
